entries.evidence: A cairn and a dam imply different features. Puech prefers a cairn; the dam proposal must be checked independently.
entries.caution: The proposed Qumran dam is reconstructed. Neither it nor a particular cairn has been established as this entry’s landmark.

entries.title: Sekakah
entries.description: The head of a water conduit associated with Sekakah; the link and stone landmark are partly restored.
entries.evidence: Qumran’s water system supplies a plausible conduit-head setting. Ilan–Amit’s 1989 plan puts the visible intake beside a reconstructed dam. Stacey (2007) dates the main aqueduct after the 31 BCE earthquake and makes the dam and the cliff tunnel a later stage.
entries.caution: The link to Sekakah and the stone noun are partly restored. Northern approach and northern side must be tested separately. Under Stacey’s phasing, the earlier channel began where the aqueduct leaves the cliff, so the head of a construction stage is an alternative to the dam intake; the phasing is a hypothesis. The pin marks the settlement.
entries.landmark: the head of a water conduit
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Eshel CSS pp. 94–95; ʿAtiqot 41 preface p. viii; Milik DJD D9; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026); Lefkovits 2000 pp. 185–189; Stacey 2009, The Dam; Stacey 2007, DSD 14 pp. 222–243

entries.landmark: a fissure; a reservoir ("of Solomon")
entries.period: in use 1st c. BCE–70 CE
entries.sources: Cohen & Porat, HA-ESI 132 (2020); Milik 1960 p. 147; SWP III p. 210; Puech 2006 pp. 187–189; Qumran reference review (28 September 2026)

entries.title: Bezek?
entries.description: A great conduit; the Bezek reading competes with other readings.
entries.evidence: Zertal identifies Eusebius’s two villages called Bezek, 17 miles from Neapolis, with the two Ibziq sites. A kokhim tomb excavated at Kh. Ibziq in 1971 held pottery of the 1st–2nd centuries CE, which fits Puech’s alternative “burial chamber” reading in type. Zertal places the older Bezeq at nearby Kh. Salhab.
entries.caution: Zertal’s survey reports cisterns and burial caves but no conduit at either Ibziq site, and few Early Roman sherds on the surface. The place name depends on a disputed reading.
entries.landmark: a great conduit
entries.period: partly: Roman kokhim tomb of the 1st–2nd c. CE (HA 40 p. 22); few Early Roman surface sherds (Upper Ibziq: two ER vessels illustrated; Lower Ibziq from Byzantine)
entries.sources: HA 40 (1971) p. 22; Zertal 2008 (MHCS 2) pp. 104–107, 151–153, 191–198; SWP II p. 237; see entry59_bezek_review.md and source_leads_2026-09-29.md

entries.evidence: The public site index retains these candidates for comparison. It supplies no uniquely identified landmark for this entry.
entries.caution: The placement remains at site or district level. The scroll’s individual feature has not been identified.
entries.period: Not established in the public archaeology index

places.name: Kh. Qumran (site, aqueduct, cisterns, nearby cliff caves)
Kh. Ibziq (Bezek)
places.note: Upper Kh. Ibziq, Zertal site 44 (Old Israel Grid 1878/1971). Lower Kh. Ibziq, site 42, lies 1 km north-east. Zertal reports cisterns, burial caves and a Roman road, but no conduit. A kokhim tomb of the 1st–2nd centuries CE was excavated at Kh. Ibziq in 1971 (HA 40 p. 22). Not a feature location.
places.source: Wikidata Q49354325 (Khirbet Ibziq); Q31248544 is the modern village 4.0 km SW

places.name: Upper Beth-Horon (Beit ʿUr el-Foqa)
places.note: Village anchor from the IAA Benjamin survey (sites 28/143). Lower Beth-Horon (Beit ʿUr et-Taḥta) is equally compatible and has the only tomb with pottery of the period. Not a feature location.
places.source: IAA survey, Ramallah–Benjamin map 83/1, sites 28 and 143

places.name: Kh. Salhab (Kh. es-Selhab)
places.note: Tell 3 km WSW of Upper Kh. Ibziq on the Neapolis–Scythopolis road. Zertal identifies it as biblical Bezeq (1 Sam 11:8) and holds that the name later moved to Ibziq. Early Roman pottery 15%; no conduit reported. Not a feature location.
places.source: Zertal 2008, Manasseh Hill Country Survey 2, site 23 (Israel grid 1853/1957), converted to WGS84 from EPSG:28193 with pyproj; the same conversion puts Upper Ibziq about 230 m from its atlas anchor
